elements.element: Customer owns Deliverables and work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: Revised 14.2: "Customer exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer"; "Deliverable" is defined (1.4) to include each report, configuration, integration, specification, design, workflow, training material "and other work product that an Order Form identifies as being created specifically for Customer," so work product is captured.

elements.element: Vendor assigns the Deliverables and work product to Customer.
elements.evidence: Revised 14.2: "Vendor hereby assigns to Customer all right, title, and interest in each Deliverable" — a present-tense assignment covering the defined Deliverables (which include work product).

elements.element: Vendor retains its pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: 14.3 (retained): "Vendor retains Vendor Technology"; 1.8 defines Vendor Technology as "Vendor's pre-existing software, tools, models, templates, documentation, routines, connectors, and other technology," excluding Customer Data and Customer's pre-Effective Date IP.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Vendor IP embedded in Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: 13.2 (unchanged): for Vendor Technology "embedded in a Deliverable, Vendor grants Customer and its Affiliates a perpetual ... licence"; 14.3 confirms "the perpetual licence in Section 13.2 applies" to Vendor Technology incorporated in a Deliverable.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: 13.2: "a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence."

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: 13.2: "royalty-free, fully paid licence to use, execute, reproduce, display, perform, modify, create derivative works from, and permit contractors to support that material for Customer's business."

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: 14.1: "As between the Parties, Customer owns all Customer Data, Customer Confidential Information, Customer-provided material, and intellectual property Customer owned or developed independently of the Services."

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: 14.1: "No right transfers to Vendor except the limited right to process that material solely to provide, secure, support, and improve the Services for Customer." Securing, supporting and improving the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation; no resale/distribution or broader "purposes contemplated" right appears.

elements.element: The parties do not jointly own intellectual property.
elements.evidence: 14.4: "No jointly owned intellectual property is created unless the Parties sign a separate instrument identifying it and their exploitation rights." Default is no joint ownership, and any future joint IP requires a signed instrument specifying exploitation rights, so the walk-away (joint ownership without exploitation rights) cannot arise unilaterally.

elements.element: Vendor may retain ownership of generic tools and know-how.
elements.evidence: 14.3 "Vendor retains Vendor Technology" (tools, models, templates, routines per 1.8), and 1.4 excludes from Deliverables "generally applicable ideas, methods, skills, and know-how retained in the unaided memory of Vendor personnel."

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Condition superseded: revised 14.2 vests exclusive ownership of each Deliverable in Customer by present assignment, which confers rights of unlimited duration greater than any licence; no residual term limit survives because the old "revocable ... only during the applicable Order Form term" sentence was deleted.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: Superseded by ownership under revised 14.2 ("Vendor hereby assigns to Customer all right, title, and interest in each Deliverable"); the previously retained "revocable" licence language is removed, so nothing permits Vendor revocation.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is worldwide.
elements.evidence: Ownership under revised 14.2 is unqualified as to territory, and embedded Vendor Technology carries an express "worldwide" licence under 13.2.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: Revised 14.2 imposes no further payment for Customer's ownership rights, and 13.2 makes the embedded Vendor Technology licence "royalty-free, fully paid."

elements.element: Customer may use and modify Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: As exclusive owner under revised 14.2 Customer may use and modify; 13.2 separately permits Customer to "modify, create derivative works from" embedded Vendor Technology "for Customer's business."

elements.element: Customer may sublicense Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: Exclusive ownership plus assignment of "all right, title, and interest" in revised 14.2 includes the right to license out; no retained restriction on transfer survives (the "non-transferable" licence sentence was deleted).

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: 14.1 second sentence limits Vendor to "the limited right to process that material solely to provide, secure, support, and improve the Services for Customer."

elements.element: Customer owns Deliverables and work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: Duplicate check of revised 14.2 confirms Customer ownership plus assignment; no contrary retained sentence remains in Section 14.

reasons: The single operation rewrites only Section 14.2, the one clause that failed the playbook (Vendor exclusive ownership with a revocable, term-limited, non-transferable licence back). Deleting the old second sentence was necessary, not cosmetic: a revocable Order-Form-term licence to Customer would directly contradict the new Customer ownership.

Preferred level is complete on the operative text: ownership plus present assignment (14.2 as revised), Vendor retains pre-existing IP (14.3 with 1.8), perpetual/irrevocable/royalty-free (and worldwide, fully paid) licence to embedded Vendor Technology (13.2, cross-referenced by 14.3), Customer Data ownership with Vendor limited to service-delivery processing (14.1), and no default joint ownership (14.4).

No new Vendor rights were created: nothing assigns Customer IP or Customer Data to Vendor, and the Vendor Data right remains "solely to provide, secure, support, and improve the Services for Customer," which is service delivery rather than independent exploitation.

Intent is preserved: the 14.3 cross-reference to "the perpetual licence in Section 13.2" still resolves, the Vendor Technology identification and third-party-material approval protections survive, and the feedback mechanics in 14.4 are untouched. No dangling defined term or orphan cross-reference results.
No extras were added — no survival tail, indemnity, escrow, moral-rights waiver, further-assurances covenant, or expense allocation — so the redline stays inside the IP checklist.

Optional polish only (do not treat as a defect): the drafter could add "and all work product" after "Deliverable" in 14.2 for clarity, but the 1.4 definition already sweeps in Order-Form-identified work product, so the current wording is sufficient.
